blocks.text: NOx takes part in a series of reactions leading to ozone, aldehydes, peroxyacyl nitrates (PANs) and peroxybenzoyl nitrate (PBN). PAN is one member of the peroxyacyl nitrates, general structure RC(O)OONO2 (Figure 12.4); in peroxyacetyl nitrate R is CH3, but other hydrocarbon chains may be present. The formation of PAN (Figure 12.5): the main component of oxidising smog is ozone, which oxidises a hydrocarbon to an aldehyde; the aldehyde reacts with a hydroxyl radical to give an acyl radical; the acyl radical reacts with oxygen to give a peroxyacyl radical, which finally reacts with nitrogen dioxide to form peroxyacyl nitrate.

blocks.alt: The structure R-C(=O)-O-O-NO2 drawn as a zigzag: an acyl group RC(O)- with a C=O, a peroxy link -O-O-, and a nitro group in which nitrogen carries a + charge, a double-bonded oxygen and an O- oxygen. Brackets name the three parts. A box gives the general formula RC(O)OONO2 and says R = CH3 gives peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN).
blocks.caption: General structure of PANs (original diagram after Figure 12.4).

blocks.alt: A reaction cycle. A reactive hydrocarbon (with O3) gives the radical RCH2.; + O2 gives RCH2O2.; + NO gives RCH2O. + NO2; + O2 gives RCHO + HO2; HO2 + NO gives HO. + NO2; HO. + RCH3 gives RCH2. again. Below, the aldehyde RCHO + HO. gives the acyl radical RC.=O, + O2 gives the peroxyacyl radical RC(O)OO., and + NO2 gives PAN, RC(O)OONO2.
blocks.caption: Mechanism of PAN formation (original diagram after Figure 12.5).
